title: THE MASTER COMPENDIUM: OPHTHALMIC GRADING & CLASSIFICATIONS
summary: An exhaustive clinical resource mapping diagnostic criteria, staging systems, and severity scales across all ophthalmic subspecialties—from retinal dystrophies to orbital inflammation. Designed for board-certified mastery and rapid clinical reference.

sections.title: DEDICATION & FOREWORD
sections.content: Grading in ophthalmology. This work is dedicated to my father osama ahmed el barchoumi please don’t forget to pray for him and read al fateha.

rows: Round sharply delineated, egg yolk appearance within RPE
Part of lesion regress at puberty; fluid level within lesion
OCT: Material beneath, above, within RPE
Lesion breaks up ('scrambled egg'); visual acuity drops
Subnormal EOG continues; variable FA staining
Residual attachment of vitreous within 3mm radius of central macula.
Perifoveal vitreomacular separation present; OCT: Observed appearance.
Perifoveal within 3mm PVD (not associated with vitromacular disease).
Retinal changes in OCT; distortion of inner retina with photoreceptor apposition.
Interruption of all retinal layers from ILM to RPE +/- VMT.
Categorized as Small, Medium, or Large (>400μm).
Partial thickness defect at inner retinal layers at the fovea.
Lesion mimics FTMH; distortion of perifoveal retina into heaped up edges by ERM.
No loss of retinal layers; thickness near normal; defect in ERM only.

sections.title: Gass Classification of Clinical Macular Hole
content: Stage 1a: Impending hole (Foveal flattening + underlying yellow spot)
Stage 1b: Occult hole (Foveal detachment + yellow ring)
Stage 2: Small FTMH (<400 microns); Defect: central, eccentric, or crescentic shape
Stage 3: FTMH > 400 microns with no vitreous separation
Stage 4: FTMH > 400 microns with vitreous separation (Complete PVD)

sections.title: Vitreous Haze Grading
content: Grade 0: Good view of Nerve Fiber Layer (NFL)
Grade +1: Clear disc and vessels but hazy NFL
Grade +2: Disc and vessels appear hazy
Grade +3: Only the optic disc is visible
Grade +4: Optic disc is not visible

sections.title: RAPD Grading Details
content: Grade 1 (0.4 log unit): Weak initial restriction followed by greater redilation
Grade 2 (0.7 log unit): Initial stalling followed by greater redilation
Grade 3 (1.1 log unit): Immediate dilation
Grade 4 (2 log unit): Immediate dilation following prolonged illumination of the good eye for 6 seconds
Grade 5 (Infinity): Immediate dilation with no secondary constriction

sections.title: Angle Grading: Van Herick & Shaffer Systems

rows: Incapable of closure; Scleral spur visible
Closed; Iridocorneal contact; No structures identified

branches: Spaeth System: Iris insertion, Angular approach, Peripheral iris curvature
Scheie System: The opposite of Shaffer

sections.title: Hypertensive Retinopathy
content: Grade 1: Mild generalized arteriolar narrowing
Grade 2: Focal arteriolar narrowing + A.V. nipping (Copper wiring appearance)
Grade 3: Grade 2 + retinal hemorrhage, exudate, and cotton wool spots
Grade 4: Grade 3 + Optic disc swelling

rows: Peripheral AV anastomosis proximal to non-perfused areas
Sea fan neovascularization at edges of perfused retina
Optic disc sign: Dark red blots due to small vessel occlusion
Macular retinal depression sign; peripheral color changes

sections.title: Retinopathy of Prematurity (ROP)
content: Zone 1: Radius 2x distance from disc to center of macula.
Zone 2: From edge of Zone 1 to nasal ora serrata.
Zone 3: Residual temporal crescent anterior to Zone 2.
Stage 1: Demarcation line (thin, flat, white line parallel to ora).
Stage 2: Demarcation ridge (height and width; vessels enter the ridge).
Stage 3: Extraretinal fibrovascular proliferation (into vitreous; peak incidence ~35 weeks PCA).
Stage 4: Partial RD (4A: Extrafoveal, 4B: Foveal).
Stage 5: Total Retinal Detachment.
Plus Disease: Dilatation/tortuosity in at least 2 quadrants of posterior fundus.
Rush Disease (Aggressive ROP): Rapidly progressive in Zones 1/2 with prominent Plus disease.

sections.title: Proliferative Vitreoretinopathy (PVR)
content: Type A (Minimal): Vitreous haze, pigment (tobacco dust) on inner retina.
Type B (Moderate): Retinal wrinkling, stiffening, rolled edges of breaks, vessel tortuosity.
Type C (Marked): Rigid retinal folds (starfolds), heavy vitreous condensation/strands.
Subtypes of C: Location (Pre-equatorial/Post-equatorial), Extent, Contraction Type (Focal, Diffuse, Subretinal, Circumferential, Anterior).

rows: None or few small drusen (<63 microns)
Multiple small drusen; few intermediate (63-124μm); RPE abnormalities
Extensive intermediate drusen; at least one large druse (>/=125μm); Geographic atrophy (no fovea)
Geographic atrophy involving fovea or Neovascular AMD features

sections.title: Clinical Staging: Aging vs AMD
content: Normal Aging: Only drupelets; No AMD pigmentary abnormalities.
Early AMD: Medium drusen (>63 but <125 microns); No pigmentary abnormalities.
Intermediate AMD: Large drusen (>125) or any AMD pigmentary abnormalities.
Late AMD: Neovascular AMD and/or any geographic atrophy.

sections.title: Retinal Angiomatous Proliferation (RAP)
content: Stage 1: Intraretinal NV; Telangiectatic vessels; small angiomatous lesions.
Stage 2: Subretinal NV; Extension into subretinal space; Edema/Exudates; Serous PED may exist.
Stage 3: Macular Neovessels; Perfusion via choroid + retinochoroidal anastomosis; evident clinically/angiographically.

rows: Total epithelial loss; Stromal haze; 1/3-1/2 ischemia

sections.title: Hyphema & Papilledema
content: Hyphema Grade 1: <= 1/3 AC volume.
Hyphema Grade 2: 1/3 - 1/2 AC volume.
Hyphema Grade 3: > 1/2 AC volume.
Hyphema Grade 4: Total volume (8-ball hyphema); Microhyphema: circulating cells only.
Papilledema Grade 0: Normal disc.
Papilledema Grade 1: Minimal; subtle C-shaped halo; normal temporal margin.
Papilledema Grade 2: Low degree; circumferential halo.
Papilledema Grade 3: Moderate; obscuration of 1+ major vessels leaving disc.
Papilledema Grade 4: Marked; partial obscuration of major vessels ON the disc.
Papilledema Grade 5: Severe; total obscuration of all vessels on the disc.

branches: NOSPEC: No signs (0), Only signs (1), Soft tissue (2), Proptosis (3), EOM (4), Corneal (5), Sight loss (6)
VISA: Vision (Optic Nerve), Inflammation, Strabismus, Appearance (Lid retraction/proptosis)
EUGOGO Activity: Spontaneous pain, Pain on gaze, Redness of eyelids, Swelling of conjunctiva/plica/lid, Chemosis
EUGOGO Severity: Mild (Minor impact), Mod-Severe (Lid >2mm, Proptosis >3mm, Diplopia), Sight Threatening (Optic neuropathy, Corneal breakdown)
Mourits Score: Lid edema/injection, Conjunctival chemosis/injection, Pain on movement. Score >=4 = Active.
Randle Curve: Active phase -> Regression phase -> Inactive plateau.

sections.title: Ocular Surface & Infections
content: WHO Trachoma: TF (Follicles >0.5mm), TI (Intense inflammation), TS (Scarring), TT (Trichiasis), CO (Corneal Opacity).
WHO Xerophthalmia: XN (Night blindness), X1 (Xerosis/Bitot), X2 (Corneal xerosis), X3 (Ulcer <1/3 A; >1/3 B), XS (Scar), XF (Fundus).
Neurotrophic Keratopathy: Stage 1 (Epithelial irregularity), Stage 2 (PED with rolled edges), Stage 3 (Stromal melting).
OCP (Foster): Stage 1 (Chronic conjunctivitis/fibrosis), Stage 2 (Forniceal shortening), Stage 3 (Symblepharon), Stage 4 (Ankyloblepharon).
OCP (Mondino): Inferior forniceal depth loss: Stage 1 (<25%), 2 (25-50%), 3 (50-75%), 4 (>75%).
Chandler (Sinus): 1 (Preseptal), 2 (Postseptal), 3 (Subperiosteal abscess), 4 (Orbital abscess), 5 (Cavernous sinus thrombosis).

sections.title: Vitreoretinal Degenerations & Phthisis
content: Atrophia Bulbi: Grade 1 (No shrinkage), Grade 2 (Shrinkage), Grade 3 (Disorganization/Phthisis), Grade 4 (Ossification), Grade 5 (Calcium deposition).
FEVR: Stage 1 (Peripheral avascularity), Stage 2 (NV/Exudates), Stage 3 (Macula sparing RD), Stage 4 (Macula involving RD), Stage 5 (Total RD).
Snowflake Degeneration: Stage 1 (White-without-pressure <15y), Stage 2 (Crystalline deposits 15-25y), Stage 3 (Vascular sheathing 25-50y), Stage 4 (Atrophy/Pigment >60y).
North Carolina Dystrophy: Grade 1 (Drusen-like; asymptomatic), Grade 2 (Confluent deposits; guarded), Grade 3 (Atrophic macular lesions; low VA).
